# Environment setup + data cleaning

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(plotly)
library(htmlwidgets)
library(ggiraph)
library(patchwork)
library(sf)

source("./utils.R")
```

Here, we're removing the duplicates from our analysis.

```{r}
flock_df <- read.csv("../data/flock_combined_24-26.csv") %>% 
  filter(duplicate_likely == FALSE) %>% 
  select(-dup1_check,
         -dup2_check,
         -duplicate_likely)

nrow(flock_df)
```

```{r}
# Step 1: extract the state data from Org.Name
flock_df$state_pd <- sapply(flock_df$Org.Name, extract_state)
```

# Interactive Visualizations

## Immigration searches over time

### Entire dataset timeline

NOTE: Make sure that it doesn't care about letter casing here.

```{r}
# filter out the immigration related stuff
IMMIGRATION_KEYWORD <- "immigration|border( patrol)+|homeland security( investigation)+|WARRANT/FUGITIVE\\) - HSI|\\bi.c.e.\\b|\\busbp\bb|\\bcbp\\b"
# IMMIGRATION_AGENCIES <- "border patrol|immigration|\\bi.c.e.\\b|\\busbp\\b|\\bcbp\\b"

flock_immigration <- flock_df %>% 
  mutate(immigration_search = grepl(IMMIGRATION_KEYWORD, Reason, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>% 
         # immigration_agency = grepl(IMMIGRATION_AGENCIES, Org.Name, ignore.case = TRUE),
         # immigration = (immigration_search | immigration_agency)) %>% 
  filter(immigration_search == TRUE)
```

This plots the number of searches conducted per month over time for the immigration-related searches.
```{r}
time_hist <- flock_immigration %>% 
  mutate(search_month_year = floor_date(as.Date(Search.Time), unit="month")) %>% 
  group_by(search_month_year) %>% 
  summarize(n_searches = n()) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = search_month_year, y = n_searches)) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "3 months", date_labels = "%m %Y") +
  ggtitle("Immigration-related searches of Springfield's Flock data") +
  geom_col_interactive(fill = "dodgerblue3") +
  theme(text = element_text(size=8),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle=45)) +
  labs(x = "", y = "",
       caption = "Immigration-related searches of Springfield’s Flock data, per month. \nSource: Flock Safety network audits for Springfield PD, January 2024 to October 2026, obtained by \nthe ACLU of Massachusetts under the Massachusetts Public Records Law.")

# 2. Convert it into an interactive Plotly chart
# interactive_chart <- ggplotly(time_hist)
interactive_chart <- girafe(ggobj = time_hist)

time_hist

# 3. Export and download as a self-contained HTML file
saveWidget(interactive_chart, file = "../figs/n_immigration_searches.html", selfcontained = TRUE)
# htmltools::save_html(interactive_chart, "../figs/n_immigration_searches.html", selfcontained = TRUE)
```

## Searches geographically
Next, let's work on the choropleth that maps out the states with access to this data.

#### Pre 2026

```{r}
state_counts_pre_2026 <- flock_df %>% 
  filter(!is.na(state_pd),
         Org.Name != "Springfield MA PD",
         Search.Time < as.Date("2026-01-01")) %>%
  group_by(state_pd) %>% 
  summarize(n_searches = n()) %>% 
  arrange(desc(n_searches))
```

```{r}
# Step 2: generate histogram 
state_hist <- state_counts_pre_2026 %>% 
  head(n=10) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(state_pd, n_searches),
             y = n_searches,
             tooltip = paste(state_pd, ": ", n_searches),
             data_id = n_searches)) +
  geom_col_interactive(stat = "identity",
                       fill = "steelblue2") +
  coord_flip() + 
  theme_minimal(base_size = 6) +
  labs(title = "Top 10 states whose police searched Springfield's Flock data most, \nJan 2024 - Dec 2025",
       x = "state",
       y = "# of searches in database",
       caption = "Searches of Springfield's Flock data by police in each state, excluding Springfield PD, Jan 2024 - Dec 2025. \nSource: Flock Safety network audits for Springfield PD, January 2025 to October 2026, \nobtained by the ACLU of Massachusetts Public Records Law.")

state_hist
```

```{r}
# Step 3: generate choropleth
us_sf <- read_sf("../data/cb_2018_us_state_20m/cb_2018_us_state_20m.shp") %>% 
  filter(STUSPS != "AK",
         STUSPS != "HI",
         STUSPS != "PR")

state_sf_counts <- left_join(us_sf,
                             state_counts_pre_2026,
                             by = c("STUSPS" = "state_pd"))

state_sf_counts$n_searches <- state_sf_counts$n_searches %>% 
  replace_na(0)

counts_map <- state_sf_counts %>% 
  mutate(binned_counts = cut(n_searches,
                             breaks = c(0, 500000, 1000000, 2000000),
                             include.lowest = TRUE,
                             labels = c("0 - 500,000", "500,000 - 1,000,000", "1,000,000 - 2,000,000"))) %>% 
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(size=0.5) +
  geom_sf_interactive(aes(fill = binned_counts,#n_searches,
                          tooltip = paste(NAME, ": ", n_searches),
                          data_id = n_searches)) + 
  theme_void(base_size = 6) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "# of searches, binned", # Optional: change legend title
    values = c(
      "0 - 500,000" = "slategray1",
      "500,000 - 1,000,000" = "steelblue2",
      "1,000,000 - 2,000,000" = "steelblue4"
    )
  ) +
  labs(title = "Searches of Springfield's Flock data by police in each state, Jan 2024 - Dec 2025")

counts_map
```

```{r}
combined_plot <- counts_map + free(state_hist) + plot_layout(ncol = 1)

interactive_plot <- girafe(ggobj = combined_plot)
interactive_plot <- girafe_options(
  interactive_plot,
  opts_hover(css = "fill:orange;stroke:black;")
)

# save as an html widget
saveWidget(interactive_plot, file = "../figs/state-pd-counts_pre_2026.html", selfcontained = TRUE)
# htmltools::save_html(interactive_plot, "../figs/state-pd-counts_pre_2026.html", selfcontained = TRUE)
```

```{r}
interactive_plot
```

# Fact-checking the prose

Federal agencies searched Springfield’s Flock data directly, including Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), which is part of ICE, and the U.S. Border Patrol. 
```{r}
flock_df %>% 
  filter(grepl("federal", Org.Name, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>% 
  select(Org.Name) %>% 
  unique()
```

Police nationwide searched Springfield’s Flock data nearly 1,500 times for reasons citing ICE, HSI, Customs and Border Protection, Border Patrol, or immigration.
```{r}
nrow(flock_immigration)
```

Police have used Flock to search for people, not just cars, in searches that reached Springfield’s cameras. 
- "On April 8, 2026, the Providence, Rhode Island police department ran one such search that reached Springfield’s cameras. It was labeled “[people] lime green hoodie and green checkered pajama pants pushing scooter.”
- There's a bigger picture here: they are actually able to get around Flock's moderation by simply changing the 'people' in the original search to 'vehicle'.
```{r}
flock_df %>% 
  filter(Search.Time == as.Date("04-08-2026",
                                format = "%m-%d-%Y"),
         state_pd == "RI") %>% 
  filter(grepl("lime green hoodie and green checkered pajama pants pushing scooter", Text.Prompt, ignore.case = TRUE))
```

Police nationwide, and Springfield officers themselves, have searched Springfield’s Flock data in connection with protests and political rallies. 
```{r}
flock_df %>% 
  filter(grepl("protest|rally", Reason, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>% 
  select(Org.Name) %>% 
  unique()
```

Between January 2024 and early December 2025, agencies outside of Springfield searched Springfield’s Flock data more than 9 million times.
```{r}
sum(state_counts_pre_2026$n_searches)
```

Immigration-related searches of Springfield’s Flock data peaked in March 2025, with 4,305 searches by 220 agencies in 39 states.
```{r}
flock_immigration %>% 
  filter(between(Search.Time, as.Date("2025-03-01"), as.Date("2025-03-31"))) %>% 
  select(state_pd) %>% 
  unique() %>% 
  count()
```


Homeland Security Investigations account ran 172 searches between March and May. 
```{r}
flock_df %>% 
  filter(between(Search.Time, as.Date("2025-03-01"), as.Date("2025-05-31")),
         grepl("Homeland Security Investigation", Org.Name, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>% 
  count()
```

U.S. Border Patrol accounts ran 201 searches in May and June. 
```{r}
flock_df %>% 
  filter(between(Search.Time, as.Date("2025-05-01"), as.Date("2025-06-30")),
         grepl("Border Patrol", Org.Name, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>% 
  count()
```

The Naval Criminal Investigative Service ran 123. 
```{r}
flock_df %>% 
  filter(between(Search.Time, as.Date("2025-01-01"), as.Date("2025-12-31")),
         grepl("Naval Criminal Investigative Service", Org.Name, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>% 
  count()
```
In 2026, there were XXX searches from New England and New York that referenced HSI.
```{r}
flock_df %>% 
  filter(grepl("\\bhsi\\b|homeland security", Reason, ignore.case = TRUE),
         Search.Time > as.Date("2026-01-01")) %>% 
  select(state_pd) %>% 
  unique()
```

```{r}
flock_df %>% 
  filter(Search.Time > as.Date("2026-01-01"),
         grepl("\\bhsi\\b|homeland security", 
               Reason, 
               ignore.case = TRUE)) %>% 
  count()
```

The U.S. Postal Inspection Service has searched Springfield’s data more than 70,000 times since 2024, including through October 2026.
```{r}
flock_df %>% 
  filter(grepl("Postal Inspection Service", Org.Name, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>% 
  count()
```
```{r}
flock_df %>% 
  filter(grepl("Postal Inspection Service", Org.Name, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>% 
  select(Search.Time) %>% 
  unique()
```


Police in Braintree, Massachusetts; Nashua, New Hampshire N.H.; and Norwalk, Connecticut. ran similar searches for people between October 2025 and June 2026. 
- this is correct
```{r}
people_searches %>% 
  filter(Text.Prompt != "", 
         !is.na(Text.Prompt), 
         grepl("person|people", Text.Prompt)) %>% 
  select(Org.Name, Text.Prompt)
```

Between January 2024 and early October 2026, agencies outside of Springfield searched Springfield’s Flock data more than 10.5 million times, mining information collected by Springfield’s dozens of Flock cameras.
```{r}
flock_df %>% 
  filter(!grepl("Springfield", Org.Name, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>% 
  count()
```
In 2025 alone, police in Texas searched Springfield’s Flock data more than 1.1 million times. 
```{r}
flock_df %>% 
  filter(between(Search.Time, as.Date("2025-01-01"), as.Date("2026-12-31")),
         state_pd == "TX") %>% 
  count()
```
Police in Florida, where state law requires local law enforcement to take part in civil immigration enforcement, searched the records more than 425,000 times. 
```{r}
flock_df %>% 
  filter(between(Search.Time, as.Date("2025-01-01"), as.Date("2026-21-31")),
         state_pd == "FL") %>% 
  count()
```

Those nationwide lookups stopped around February 10, 2026, and most outside searches since then have come from New England and New York. 
```{r}
flock_df %>% 
  filter(state_pd != "MA") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = floor_date(Search.Time, unit = "month"))) +
  geom_bar()
```

```{r}
flock_df %>% 
  filter(state_pd != "MA",
         Search.Time > as.Date("2026-02-10")) %>% 
  group_by(state_pd) %>% 
  summarize(count = n()) 
```
The most recent search explicitly naming ICE’s deportation operations was conducted on July 10, 2026, at 7:39 a.m. by an officer with the Barnstable, Massachusetts police department. In the reason field, the officer wrote “Wanted Person (Arrest Warrant/Fugitive) – warrants/ERO.” It wasn’t the first time: on November 2, 2025, Barnstable police ran five searches with the reason “Ero.”
- both are correct
```{r}
flock_ero <- flock_df %>% 
  filter(grepl("ERO", Reason, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>% 
  arrange(Search.Time)
```

More recently, in September 2026, two New York agencies searched Springfield’s Flock data for reasons citing HSI. They were among thousands of HSI-related searches in Springfield’s audits.
```{r}
flock_df %>% 
  filter(grepl("homeland security|hsi", Reason, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>% 
  count()
```
Immigration-related searches of Springfield’s Flock data peaked in March 2025, with 4,884 searches by 250 agencies in 42 states.
- it's actually 4,305 searches, 220 agencies, 39 states
```{r}
flock_immigration_2026 %>% 
  filter(between(as.Date("2025-03-01"), as.Date("2025-03-31"), Search.Time), #between(Search.Time, as.Date("2025-01-01"), as.Date("2026-01-01")),
         !is.na(state_pd)) %>% 
  select(state_pd) %>%
  unique() %>%
  nrow()
  # summarize(n_searches = nrow(.),
  #           n_agencies = nrow(unique(Org.Name)),
  #           n_states = nrow(unique(state_pd)))
```

Searches naming immigration-related keywords declined sharply after February 2026, but HSI-related searches continued at about 50 a month through the summer.
```{r}
flock_df %>% 
  filter(Search.Time >= as.Date("2026-03-01"),
         grepl(IMMIGRATION_KEYWORD, Reason, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>% 
  mutate(month_time = floor_date(Search.Time, unit = "month")) %>% 
  group_by(month_time) %>% 
  count()
```

Between January 2024 and early October 2026, police searched Springfield’s Flock data more than 140 times in connection with protests or political rallies.
```{r}
flock_df %>% 
  filter(grepl("protest|rally", Reason, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>% 
  count()
```
In a single day, July 4, 2025, the Lubbock, Texas police department ran 54 searches labeled “protest [].”
```{r}
flock_df %>% 
  filter(Search.Time == as.Date("2025-07-04"),
         state_pd == "TX",
         grepl("protest", Reason, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>% 
  count()
```
On February 19, 2024, SPD officer Haley Radisic ran six searches on two license plates labeled “Palestinian Protest 02-19-2024.” 
```{r}
flock_df %>% 
  filter(Search.Time == as.Date("2024-02-19"),
         grepl("palestinian protest", Reason, ignore.case = TRUE)) 
```

On October 13, 2024, officer Olivia Malone ran two searches of one license plate, writing “protest” as the reason. 
```{r}
flock_df %>% 
  filter(Search.Time == as.Date("2024-10-13"),
         grepl("protest", Reason, ignore.case = TRUE)) 
```
